messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 runtime instability in eu-central-1: multiple GPU nodes flapping; symptoms include CUDA ILLEGAL READ/WRITE, container crashes, progressive KV cache growth and paged-attention fragmentation. Autoscaler reacting. Refer: https://alerts.internal/INC-20260314-77

alice: saw spike in 02:10-02:35Z window. several pods on gpu-pool-9 restarted repeatedly with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then OOM from paged allocator.

ben: pulling logs from node gpu-node-09-03. snippet:
```
2026-03-14T02:18:42Z runtime[pid=3101]: attention_pager: page fault remapped -> slab leak
2026-03-14T02:18:43Z runtime[pid=3101]: kv-cache: allocated 9.1GB -> 10.7GB (+1.6GB/8m)
2026-03-14T02:18:43Z runtime[pid=3101]: cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7f8a... in aten_kernel
2026-03-14T02:18:44Z runtime[pid=3101]: SIGKILL sent: OOM killer invoked
```

cory: correlation with long chat sessions and many short sequences that keep unique attention windows. Eviction threshold not aggressive enough; many small pinned slabs from legacy session pinning code.

alice: impact: degraded p50/p95 for dedicated customers in eu-central-1, a few customers saw retries/timeouts. CS notified. Dana, update customers?

dana: messaging queued. offering reprovision to different region for any affected tenant. no enterprise customers impacted yet.

ben: temp mitigations I'm applying: 1) cordon/drain most unstable nodes, 2) set runtime env RUNTIME_KV_MAX_GROWTH_MB=300 and RUNTIME_KV_EVICT_FACTOR=0.95, 3) disable paged-attention for model-group `mix-large-enc` to see if crashes stop. executing drain now.

incident-bot: user ben cordoned gpu-node-09-03 at 2026-03-14T02:23:01Z

ben: running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-09-03 -n redwood-runtime
kubectl drain gpu-node-09-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n redwood-runtime
kubectl set env deploy/runtime RUNTIME_KV_EVICT_FACTOR=0.95 -n redwood-runtime
kubectl set env deploy/mix-large-enc RUNTIME_PAGED_ATTENTION=false -n models
```

cory: after one pod restarted, kv size dropped from ~11.2GB -> 5.5GB on that pod. fragmentation metric still high: slab-frag-ratio ~0.78.

ben: no further CUDA illegal access logs in last 10m. autoscaler scaled down extra nodes as load dropped.

alice: infra, please collect kernel logs and core dumps from nodes 09-03, 09-07, 09-11 for root cause. tag them to the postmortem.

infra-oncall: copying dmesg, /var/crash and nv-hostengine logs to secure bucket: s3://redwood-internal/dumps/2026-03-14/eu-central-1/

cory: theory: allocator fragmentation creates holes, CUDA kernel later touches reclaimed memory -> illegal access. likely exacerbated by long-lived pinned small allocations from session caching.

ben: immediate follow-ups: add emergency cache-trim endpoint (admin API) to force full eviction and slab compaction, new alert for kv growth >400MB/10m, background slab defrag work item. assigning to eng-runtime.

alice: calling this stable if no new node flaps for 30m. keep watch. update runbook with exact commands we ran.

dana: CS sent update at 02:45Z. customers acknowledged mitigations and ETA for postmortem.

incident-bot: incident marked STABLE at 2026-03-14T03:05:12Z by ben

(changelog)
- cordoned/drained nodes: gpu-node-09-03,09-07
- env changes: RUNTIME_KV_EVICT_FACTOR=0.95, RUNTIME_PAGED_ATTENTION=false for mix-large-enc
- rolling restarts one pod at a time
- CS notifications sent
- follow-ups: emergency cache-trim API, slab defrag task, kv-growth alert
